text:
Talia: Noticing repeated P95 spikes in us-west-2 rack-14 for short gens, starts ~03:22 UTC. Fractional-dedicated evicts -> spills to shared -> cascade.
Ben: same alert. NVLINK TX and PCIe write_stalls spike before NIC tx bursts. Looks like a PCIe bottleneck that then saturates NIC queues.
Ivo: any recent batch waves landing on rack-14?
Talia: yes, nightly bulk-encode started at 03:15 and a couple of jobs landed on rack-14 hosts.
Meera: quick mitigation idea: host-level pacer (eBPF) on best-effort cgroup + short cohort backoff so evicted tenants don't get requeued to the same rack for 90s.
Sam: agree. Also we should canary a small carveout lane for high-SLA tenants (2% capacity) to see if isolating them reduces tail without big cost.
Ivo: carving 2% sounds low overhead, but carveouts increase fragmentation. We should simulate expected slot-hours and cost delta before committing.
Ben: immediate steps I can run now: apply pacer to the 5 hosts in rack-14 and set cohort_backoff to 90s. If stable, start a 2% carveout canary.
Talia: go for it. Commands: 
``` 
fleetctl run --hosts rack-14 "ebpf-pacer --cgroup best-effort --egress 40% --tag incident-3723456789"
kubectl patch configmap allocator-policy -n fleet --type merge -p '{"data":{"cohort_backoff_s":"90"}}'
```
oncall-bot: eBPF pacer scheduled on 5 hosts in rack-14 (tag: incident-3723456789). Allocator patch applied.
Sam: I'll start a quick cost sim for a 2% carveout using last 14 days of allocation traces and AML's cost engine. Give me 10m.
Meera: also add metric panels for pci_write_stalls, nvlink_tx_qdepth, nic_tx_qdepth, and "dedicated->shared_spill_rate" in the preemptions dashboard.
Ben: pacer applied; nvlink_tx_qdepth down ~25% in 60s, pci_write_stalls down 18% in 90s. Preemptions dropping.
Ivo: good. What's the requeue_same_rack_count doing?
Talia: down ~38% after 8m. P95 improved ~70ms for short gens.
Sam: sim results: 2% carveout for high-SLA tenants estimated to reduce tail by ~22% in this pattern but increases committed GPU slot-hours by ~6.1% in scenario where traffic stays steady; estimated $$ delta ~4.1k/day for region.
Meera: useful. We should weigh that vs the churn cost from repeated spillovers (extra slot-hours + increased token cost). Do we have a churn-driven cost estimate?
Sam: quick rough: last 24h of spillover churn in us-west-2 accounted for ~3.0% extra slot-hours and ~2.7k in incremental infra cost. If churn continues, carveout payback looks quick.
Ivo: but carveouts are persistent costs. Alternative: invest in host IO QoS (NIC shaping + PCIe-aware scheduler) which is engineering-heavy but reduces tail without committed capacity. We should present both to product/cost committee.
Ben: agree. For now, keep pacer + cohort backoff and run 2% carveout canary for 30m to collect signal. If tail drops >20% and error-rate stable then escalate to 50% canary.
Talia: canary decision sounds fine. Sam, coordinate the canary and tag billing. Also create a small trace sample of moved tenants to measure KV warmups.
Sam: will spin up canary and attach billing tag canary=carveout-3723456789. Command I plan: 
``` 
kubectl patch configmap allocator-policy -n fleet --type merge -p '{"data":{"carveout_canary":"0.02","billing_tag":"carveout-3723456789"}}'
```
Meera: note: add an alert to watch for fragmentation: dedicated_free_frag_pct drop > 5% over 30m. Rollback if fragmentation causes other regions issues.
oncall-bot: Allocator configmap patched (carveout_canary=0.02). Billing tag recorded. Incident annotation by Ben at 3723456874.
Ben: canary live. monitoring window 30m. I'll post back with metrics and cost delta.
Ivo: long-term action items: INF-7712 evaluate host IO QoS; INF-7713 simulate carveout economics across bursty vs steady traffic; INF-7714 add allocator heuristic to de-prioritize hosts with nvlink/pcie spikes for 1h.
Talia: documenting runbook: immediate = pacer + cohort_backoff; short-term = carveout canary; long-term = host IO QoS vs carveout economics. Thanks team.
Sam: early canary signal after 9m: tail P95 down ~18%, requeue_same_rack_count down ~45%, fragmentation unchanged so far. Will continue monitoring.
Meera: if we see stateful warmups pain, we should mark sticky tenants to avoid moves for next 30m.
Ben: noted. Will pause canary and rollback if error-rate > 0.5% for any affected tenant group.
Talia: thanks. I'll update incident board and open follow-ups for the INF tickets.
